Frankfurt, 1608 · Clavis, printed pp. 56–57

Modus II: from printed letters to German

Follow one worked example from the printed page through transcription and extraction to a mechanically recomputed plaintext. Every visual has an equivalent table or prose account.

No silent emendation. The retained stream decodes to 42 letters. Its opening gafz gives ichb. The resulting text differs from the 45-letter normalized Intentio, beginning at position 6. The sources of the remaining differences are unresolved.

1. Printed example

Printed evidence

Intentio Ich bitte dich komm von stund an zu mir/ es thut sehr noth.

English I beg you, come to me at once; it is very urgent.

Full p. 56, rule and wheel · Full p. 57, alphabet and example

Herzog August Bibliothek Wolfenbüttel, Fb 243 · Library image 249

German Intentio in the reading edition

2. Transcribe and extract

Transcription / repair Printed p. 56 directs the writer to begin with an empty word, then alternate. In the opening of the cover on p. 57, the decorated initial belongs to Creator. The line break in guberna has been joined and the abbreviation in consequamur expanded.

Creator generis humani aspice Deus famulos tuos Zelo rectitudinis guberna quatenus bene conuersantes consequamur

Initials from the bold alternate words: gafzgbc

Inferred operation Take the initials of the second, fourth and subsequent even-numbered cover words. For the separate significant-letter stream, read the recorded letters in order and remove the editorial separators.

The archived transcription is retained in its previous order and spelling. Its periods delimit individual letters in this edition. The printed line is set in spaced italic type. No individual human transcriber is documented here.

Transcribed dotted letters: g.a.f.z.g.b.c.p.g.a.f.h.m.k.s.m.l.q.r.s.i.b.x.l.v.s.s.k.g.r.g.q.b.s.e.q.e.t.p.m.g.r

gafzgbcpgafhmksmlqrsibxlvsskgrgqbseqetpmgr

3. Invert the printed Alphabetum

Printed evidence Each first letter is plaintext; each second letter is its printed cipher substitute.

Complete Modus II substitution table
Plainabcdefghiklmnopqrstvxz
Cipherxzabcdefghiklmnopqrstv

Inferred operation The print moves each plaintext letter two places back on its 22-letter circle. Invert the 22 printed pairs and substitute for each cipher letter in sequence.

Computed from the committed transcription:

ichbiderichkomvonstvldanzvvmitisdvgsgxroit

Printed Intentio with normalized spelling

ichbittedichkommvonstvndanzvmiresthvtsehrnoth

Lowercase the German, omit spaces and punctuation, and write u as v for comparison. Compare the two readings with the full printed page.

Plain-text account

The print supplies the substitution alphabet, the intended German message and a separate line of significant letters. Applying the inverse alphabet to the retained transcription produces ichbiderichkomvonstvldanzvvmitisdvgsgxroit. The two readings agree through ich bi. At the sixth letter the transcription gives d where the printed intention has t.

Provenance and limits
  • Frankfurt, 1608, Herzog August Bibliothek Wolfenbüttel, Fb 243. Printed p. 56 describes the shift and diagrams the circle. Printed p. 57 gives the paired alphabet, German intention, significant letters and cover.
  • AI visual collation on 23 November 2026 checked the two pages, all 22 substitutions and the first fourteen cover words. Human verification of this correction is undocumented.
  • The full significant-letter transcription is the pre-correction input. The displayed result is computed from that input without supplying letters from the printed intention.
